_comment: Hand-maintained. Every date was checked against the primary source in source_url (or the Official Journal text it cites) on verified_on; add nothing that has not been. affected_categories must match category names in data/suppliers.json exactly, or the entry shows no suppliers. Remove an entry a few months after it comes into force.

entries.title: EU packaging regulation (PPWR) applies
entries.what: The EU's packaging rules now apply directly as a regulation in every member state, replacing the 1994 packaging directive. The design duties that reach printed cartons come later: a harmonised label showing what the pack is made of from August 2028 at the earliest, and recyclability criteria from 2030.

entries.title: UK vaping duty and duty stamps start
entries.what: Vaping Products Duty is charged at £2.20 per 10ml of liquid, and products packed for retail sale must carry a vaping duty stamp. The stamp goes on the outermost retail packaging and must seal it, so pack artwork needs room for it.

entries.title: EU deforestation rules apply to paper and board
entries.what: Pulp, paper and paperboard placed on the EU market need due diligence showing the wood was legally harvested and did not come from land deforested after 2020; board made entirely from recycled fibre is exempt. For paper and board this date binds firms of every size: the December 2025 revision gave smaller firms until June 2027 only for other products, and took printed matter out of scope.

entries.title: EU: batteries in products must be user-replaceable
entries.what: Products sold in the EU with a portable battery must let the end user remove and replace it at any time in the product's life, so a vape with a sealed-in cell would not comply. Still the date in law: a simplification package under negotiation could delay it for some exempted product categories, but nothing is agreed.

entries.title: UK: every vape on sale must carry a duty stamp
entries.what: The six-month sell-through for unstamped stock ends. From this date every vaping product outside duty suspension in the UK must have a duty stamp attached, whenever it was made.

entries.title: EU ban on products made with forced labour
entries.what: No product made with forced labour may be sold in or exported from the EU, whether made inside the EU or imported. It covers every sector, so every category on the watchlist is in scope; authorities investigate suspected cases and enforce bans.

entries.title: EU supply-chain due diligence (CSDDD) applies
entries.what: Companies with more than 5,000 employees and €1.5bn turnover must identify and address human-rights and environmental harm across their chain of activities, so suppliers in every category may be asked for information. Originally due in 2027; the Omnibus I simplification adopted in 2026 moved it here and raised the thresholds.
